data.narrative:
Base Power, a Series C climate and energy company founded by Zach Dell and Justin Lopas, has raised over $1.0B to date. The valuation assessment draws on two triangulation methods applied against a comparable universe of three same-stage, same-sector private peers (KoBold Metals at $3.0B, Electric Hydrogen at $1.0B, and Amogy at $700M) alongside a broader set of eight private and one public company reference points in the climate-tech space.

The stage-progression method, applying a typical 1.7x Series C step-up multiplier to the $1.0B raised proxy, implies a valuation of $1.7B. The peer-median approach across the three identified comps yields $1.0B, reflecting the interquartile range of $700M to $3.0B observed in the peer set. These methods, when weighted equally, produce a triangulated range of $850M at the low end and $2.0B at the high end, with a median estimate of $1.4B.

Key uncertainties include the representativeness of the three-peer sample given volatility in frontier-energy valuations and the applicability of stage-progression multiples to capital-intensive, pre-revenue or early-revenue businesses in this sector. The $1.2B spread between the low and high estimates reflects material sensitivity to peer selection and assumed growth trajectory assumptions. Further diligence on Base Power's current burn rate, path to commercialization, and contract pipeline would refine this range.
